column2: A Dragon of Caledor

High in the Dragon Spine the last dragons of Caledor sleep, and each century fewer of them stir. The old secrets of the Dragon Princes are not wholly lost: with a decade of patient vigils in the smoking caves, gold for the keepers of the Dragon Shrine and a name the beasts will heed, a sleeping dragon might be woken and won as a steed.
I will climb to the caves at once.
Let the dragons sleep.

Ten years of vigils in the heat of the caves have been rewarded. An ancient dragon has opened one burning eye, heard your name and judged you worthy. It will bear you into battle as its kind once bore Caledor Dragontamer himself. Let the world know of your glory!
I am a Dragon Prince in truth!
Dragons of Caledor
Word comes from Ulthuan that [From.GetBestName] has woken one of the sleeping dragons of Caledor and now rides it to war. Let the enemies of the Asur tremble...
I thought the dragons were all asleep!
Terror from the Darkness

The oldest of the vampires know how to stitch bone, sinew and the leathery wings of great bats into a monstrous steed, and to bind it with dark magic so that it will carry its master through the night and upon his prey. It will cost much of the necromantic power you have gathered, and years of work in the crypts.
Bring me the bones.
I have better things to spend my power on.
After years of work in the crypts, the monster is finally ready. The shrieking abomination craves the blood of your enemies and will bear you wherever you wish.
Good. Now we hunt.
Flights of Devils

A knight of the Blood Dragons as mighty as you deserves a steed to match. Somewhere beyond the storm clouds run the Nightmares, dark horses that no living rider can master. The quest to find one will keep you away from your court for some years.
I ride out tonight.
Not now. Call off the quest.
There it is: a dark and twisted shape galloping through the clouds of a stormy night, eyes burning like coals. It bends to your will at last. It is time to ride home.
Home, through the storm!
A War Chariot

Since the dawn of Nehekhara, its kings have gone to war atop their chariots, and the Tomb Kings who woke from their deathly slumber lead their legions the same way. The artisans of the royal workshops can build you one worthy of your line in five years, plated in bronze and gold and drawn by skeletal steeds.
Let the workshops begin.
Not yet.
Your chariot is ready. Its armoured carriage shields you from harm, and from its high platform you can see the whole field and send your legions where they will strike hardest.
To war!
A War Mammoth

Great mammoths roam the frozen tundra of the north, where the tribes and the Ogres hunt them for meat, hides and bone. A few hunt them for war. Taking a bull alive and breaking it to the saddle is the work of years and costs many hunters, but a lord who rides one into battle can crush shield walls and batter down the gates of any stronghold.
Send the hunters north.
I will wait a while.

After five hard years, the bull mammoth is broken. It towers over even the tallest of your warriors, a howdah of furs and iron on its back and the skulls of its tamers' foes on its tusks. Your enemies will hear it long before they see it.
Let them hear us coming!
Take a War Mammoth
Send hunters into the tundra to take a bull mammoth alive and break it for war. It takes five years.

The grooms come to you with their caps in their hands. Your [dying_mount.GetName] lay down in the straw last night and did not rise again. It carried you through mud and fire and the long roads of the Old World, and now the knackers wait at the stable door.
Bury it with honour. It earned that much.
The stablemaster leads out the foal you bred, no longer a foal at all. It has grown tall and sure-footed, it takes the bit without a fight, and it will bear a rider into battle now.
Saddle it. Let us see what it can do.
